title: An IP-Agnostic Foundational Cell Array Offering Supply Chain Security
problem: IC manufacturing complexity and third-party fabrication reliance create supply chain fragility and IP security risks. Software-based configurations for general-purpose ICs are inadequate for protecting high-consequence applications.
motivation: Supply chain security and semantic IP protection are critical given manufacturing complexity and dependence on third-party foundries.
method: The FC-Array platform combines pre-tested building blocks (called standard cells) with standard chip design software (EDA tools) to enable custom chip design. It uses 3D split manufacturing—physically separating the chip design across different physical layers—so that even if someone accesses part of the design, they cannot understand or replicate its full function (called semantic IP protection). The same design supports both power-efficient operation at 100 MHz and high-performance operation at 1 GHz. Manufacturers can stockpile blank base wafers in advance, then add customized design layers when demand arrives, reducing supply chain disruption.
key_novelty: The core innovation is a chip platform that protects designs from being copied by splitting them across separate physical layers (3D split manufacturing) while reducing supply chain disruption by allowing base wafers to be manufactured and stored in advance.
contributions: IP-agnostic Foundational Cell Array platform built on verified standard cells and industry-standard EDA tools
3D split manufacturing integration to achieve semantic IP security while preserving ASIC design advantages
Base wafer stockpiling capability for supply chain resilience and manufacturing security
Demonstration of configurable power-efficient and high-performance options with quantified overheads (1.85x power, 2.61x area at 28nm)
limitations: Limitations not discussed in abstract beyond stated area and power overheads.
primary_theme: Supply chain security through 3D split manufacturing
